findings.title: website_name bypasses the TL0 anonymous-profile privacy restriction
findings.body: `website` is protected by `untrusted_attributes`, so it is omitted when an anonymous visitor views a trust-level-0 user. The new derived `website_name` attribute is not subject to that gate, and its intended inclusion method below is also not named `include_website_name?`, so the serializer still emits the hidden website's host (and, for matching domains, its path). The profile template renders this value even when `website` was withheld. Apply the same restriction to `website_name` (or implement an equivalent `include_website_name?` check) and cover anonymous TL0 serialization in the spec.

findings.title: Hostname-label comparison mistakes unrelated public-suffix domains for one domain
findings.body: The sibling-subdomain branch decides two hosts share a domain by dropping their first labels. For example, an instance at `forum.co.uk` and a profile website at `evil.co.uk/path` both reduce to `co.uk`, so the code displays the website path even though those are separately registrable, unrelated domains. The same problem occurs on shared suffixes such as `github.io`. Compare registrable domains using a public-suffix-aware mechanism, or avoid treating sibling hosts as equivalent.
